hook.text: In experiments, people pay their own money to punish cheaters—even when they'll never see them again.

buildup.text: Strong reciprocity means rewarding cooperators and punishing defectors even at personal cost. It's not rational.

discovery.text: Ernst Fehr showed this behavior is widespread: about 60% of people punish unfairness even in one-shot games.

twist.text: Punishment is contagious. When defectors see others get punished, cooperation rates jump to near 100%.

climax.text: Strong reciprocity may explain large-scale human cooperation: a few punishers keep everyone else honest.

punchline.text: Some people enforce fairness on principle.

quiz.question: What is strong reciprocity?
options: Punishing cheaters even at personal cost
